phase_evolution.value: During intercritical annealing, portions of bainite and martensite re-austenitize due to the high solubility of carbon in austenite, leading to carbon enrichment and enhanced stability; carbon-depleted regions form ferrite, some carbon-enriched austenite is retained on cooling as RA, unstabilized austenite transforms diffusionlessly to fresh martensite, and bainite forms in regions not fully austenitized.

unmapped_findings: AN800 is the intercritically annealed condition (800 °C / 30 min, air-cooled) and is distinct from AN800-T, which received an additional low-bainite aging at 400 °C for 30 min. The tensile properties reported in the paper (yield strength 985 MPa, tensile strength 1 295 MPa, elongation 18.7%) belong to AN800-T, not to this AN800 sample.

Steel critical transformation temperatures determined by dilatometry: Ac1 = 705 °C, Ac3 = 950 °C, Bf = 380 °C, Ms = 346 °C; the 800 °C annealing of AN800 lies within the Ac1–Ac3 critical region (b0149).
